description: Jasper Leijnsenstraat 11-31 and Willem de Zwijgerlaan 185-195 (BAG 1938-39): the Haringstraat ribbon-attic front with two squat attic windows per pand (instead of the ribbon) under a thick white flat eaves slab; 6.1 m red-brick fronts of five storeys with a white-framed two-over-two window pair per storey (a 2.35 m and a 1.2 m window, mirrored every pand so the windows pair across the party wall), two squat attic windows per pand under a thin white flat eaves slab at 15 m; ground: a wide window and a door (paired house doors under a light canopy) at the party wall

match.note: Leijnsenstraat 11-31 (1938, eaves 14.8-15.3 m) and Zwijgerlaan 185-195: the ribbon type's body with a pair of attic windows; faces are pinned to it (landlust-zuid-review-types.json)

flat-slab.note: Haringstraat 6-18 strip: a white eaves slab 14.4-15.0 m over the attic ribbon; flat roof

door-right.note: a 2.35 m ground window 0.75-2.4 m and the house door against the party wall (the door slot 1.2 m), a light canopy at 2.6 m over paired doors; mirrored when the strip reads the door on the left

roof.evidence: Haringstraat 6-18 strip: sky directly over the white eaves slab; 3DBAG ridge = eaves

rhythm.bays: wide + narrow window per pand, mirrored
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: window + door | 1-3: wide + narrow | 4: 2 squat attic windows
rhythm.symmetry: mirrored pairs about the party wall
rhythm.groundFloor: wide window, house door at the party wall under a canopy
rhythm.roofline: thin white flat slab over an attic ribbon

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-11-21 at 40 px/m read off the strip sheet (not gridded): wide + narrow window per storey as Haringstraat 6-18, two attic windows 1.5 m wide per pand under a 0.8 m white slab

schemaLimits: the attic ribbon's three lights per pier are drawn as one window per equal axis
the glazing bars (two over two) are simplified
the canopy over the paired doors is not drawn
notes: Palette: type default red-brown; placed pands take their trim-normalised strip wall.
